working_title: "As someone who does this for a living... no notes": deadpan green screen over a brand's slang post

research_analysis.exact_observed_hook: "So, it seems like McDonald's has came up with a new marketing strategy, and..."
research_analysis.visual_hook: A man's face in low light looking into the camera, the text "McDonald's marketing Strategy" centered, and a green-screened screenshot of a brand's own social post in front of his chest.
research_analysis.narrative_structure: One take. He introduces the brand post as a 'strategy', trails off, and under-reacts with a polite non-judgment. He never says what is odd about the image.
research_analysis.viral_mechanism: The creator withholds the joke. The viewer sees the image, gets it on their own, and the comment section becomes the place where people say it out loud.
research_analysis.observed_evidence: 2.9M views on an account with 1.8K followers, 33.0x its 88K median, 9s, zero cuts, quiet atmospheric track, no CTA. The humour in the reference depends on a suggestive reading of the brand image.
research_analysis.performance_hypothesis: Hypothesis: a nine-second clip where the punchline is left unsaid gets rewatched to confirm the reading, and viewers tag the brand or a friend. Brand posts are public and constantly renewed, so the format restocks itself.
research_analysis.why_this_format_fits_alex: Green screen plus a deadpan face is exactly his 13.5M Reel, and his best share rate came from a brand reaction (AirPods, 0.92% on TikTok). The audit found his brand-tag jokes fail when the visual is unrelated; here the brand's own post is the visual.
research_analysis.originality_changes: Borrowed: green screen over a brand's own post, polite under-reaction, joke left unsaid. New: no innuendo; the target is a serious company using stale slang, and the line is built on the fact that this is his profession.

alex_adaptation.concept: Alex stands in front of a screenshot of a serious company's social post that uses slang or a meme format far past its date. He introduces himself as a professional, offers 'no notes', waits, and then admits he has notes. He never says what they are.
alex_adaptation.target_audience: Anyone who has cringed at a brand trying to be relatable; social media managers; his existing meme audience.
alex_adaptation.first_frame: The brand's post fills the top two thirds of the frame with its handle visible. Alex is small at the bottom, eyes already on the lens, expression neutral. Centered text: '[Brand type]'s social media strategy'.
alex_adaptation.first_spoken_line: So. As someone who does this for a living.

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.dialogue: So. As someone who does this for a living.
full_script.action: Hands clasped in front of him like a consultant about to present. Neutral, respectful face. Does not look at the post.
full_script.camera: Green screen. Alex bottom-center, chest up. Screenshot of the brand post behind and above him, handle visible.
full_script.on_screen_text: a bank's social media strategy (swap 'bank' for the real category)
full_script.editing: Text on from frame one. No zooms.
full_script.audio: His voice, dry. Very quiet neutral room tone, no music.

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.action: Small, firm nod. Then he turns his head and actually looks at the post for the first time. Holds the look. His jaw tightens slightly.
full_script.editing: None. The pause is the content: hold a full two seconds of silence after the line.

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.action: Turns back to the lens. Same polite face, one notch more strained. A slow blink. He does not elaborate.
full_script.editing: Cut half a second after the blink so it loops back into 'So.'

alternate_hooks: I get paid to make content for brands, and I'd like to say one thing about this.
Somebody at this company approved this. In a meeting.
I'm 23 and even I don't say this anymore.
alternate_endings: After the long look he turns back and says, 'I would like to meet whoever approved this. To hire them.' Straight face, cut.
After the long look he says nothing at all, just slowly raises a notepad and clicks a pen. Cut.
alex_adaptation.caption: Respectfully. (screenshot from their public page)

production.location: Home, any wall; Instagram green screen
props: Notepad and pen for alternate ending 2
production.wardrobe: A collared shirt or quarter-zip so he looks like the professional in the room
shot_list: One 10-second green-screen take per screenshot; shoot three different brand screenshots in one sitting
production.editor_instructions: How to find the screenshot, any week: open the public Instagram, X or LinkedIn page of a company in a serious category (bank, insurer, airline, tax software, mattress brand) and scroll for a post that uses slang or a meme template that peaked at least six months earlier. Screenshot it with the handle and date visible. Do not edit the post. Do not say anything factual about the company: the video is opinion and the joke is his reaction. Skip posts about anything sensitive (layoffs, safety, health). Replace 'bank' in the on-screen text with the real category. Do not add music.

variants_to_test: Alternate hook: 'Somebody at this company approved this. In a meeting.'
testing.promotion_decision: Brand fit 2: promote at 48h only if views are at least 3x his trailing median and shares per 1,000 reached is top quartile; if a version with the 'for a living' line converts better than one without, keep that line in every sequel.
follow_up_variations_if_successful: Same reaction to a billboard he photographs himself while driving in Florida
Same reaction to a local business's flyer that does it right: 'No notes.' and this time he means it, and says why in the caption
Same reaction to one of his own old posts: 'I have notes.'

creative_confidence.score_type: Subjective production-priority score, not predicted viral probability
creative_confidence.rationale: Closest structural match to his biggest Reel, with the one-line addition of his profession. It can be remade weekly with a new screenshot. The laugh depends on finding a post that is funny on sight and on him holding the silence.
uncertainties: Quality of the screenshot decides the result
The audit shows his recent brand-tag memes averaged under 2,000 plays; the difference here is that the brand's post is the visual, which is a hypothesis
A brand could respond; keep it to reaction and opinion
